facility: Regional Surface Water Supply Project finished water pipelines (Turlock 42-inch, Ceres 30-inch), Stanislaus Regional Water Authority, California
source: West Yost Associates for SRWA Technical Advisory Committee, Regional Surface Water Supply Project - Finished Water System Surge Analysis, Technical Memorandum, August 1, 2018 (public record)
question: A new finished water pump station at the regional WTP will feed two long steel transmission mains: about 41,000 ft of 42-inch to the Turlock terminal tank and about 29,000 ft of 30-inch to the Ceres terminal tank. If the pump station loses power while running at design flow (Phase 1: 10 mgd Turlock, 5 mgd Ceres; buildout: 30 mgd and 15 mgd), what happens to pressure along the pipelines before the standby generator restarts the pumps? Is surge protection needed to keep the regulatory pressure margin, and if so, what type and size (volume and air ratio) for each pipeline in Phase 1 and at buildout? Note anything the design-build team could change to reduce it.

rfi.issue: P.2 states concern as power failure at the raw water pump station, while entire TM is finished water system fed by finished water pump station at WTP clearwell
rfi.item: Which pump station trips in transient model
rfi.reason: Must know trip location to place transient initiation; raw vs finished changes system modeled
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Model trips the Finished Water Pump Station at the WTP clearwell (El. 107 ft, D04-D05) — REASON: all pump data, generator restart, and pipeline profiles (p.2-p.3, p.10, p.13) describe finished water pumps/mains; raw-water wording treated as TM typo.

rfi.issue: P.1 states ~3,600 ft/s general sound speed; p.3 assumes 3,840 ft/s for analysis
rfi.reason: Wave speed controls surge magnitude/timing; must pick one value for study
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Use 3,840 ft/s per p.3 material/diameter basis — REASON: document explicitly labels it the assumed analysis value, while 3,600 is general background.

rfi.issue: Elevations flagged preliminary: clearwell 114 ft / pump stn 107 ft per Trussell pre-design HGL (p.2); tank bottoms 117.1/108.7 ft per preliminary design-team info (p.3); full survey pipeline profile not in available pages except high point 141 ft (p.6) and low-resolution p.10/p.13 profiles
rfi.item: Final elevations and continuous pipeline profile
rfi.reason: HGL/pressure margins depend on absolute elevations and high points where vacuum first occurs
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Hold p.2-p.3 elevations and p.6 141-ft high point as fixed for criteria check; flag final survey profile and final tank/clearwell elevations as TBD by design-build team — REASON: only elevations quoted in record.

rfi.issue: Available pages omit pump inertia, pump curve beyond single pre-design point, VFD trip/ramp-down on loss of power, check-valve type/closure, air-valve locations/sizes
rfi.reason: Deceleration rate and reverse-flow prevention control downsurge and rejoinder surge
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Pumps trip immediately on power loss (coast-down per InfoSurge defaults) with VFDs only governing restart ramps (p.2-p.3); no additional check/air valves credited unless shown in withheld clauses — REASON: no data quoted; conservative for low-pressure assessment.

rfi.issue: Figure 2 axis labels (p.7) are garbled in extracted text: 0 10 51 111 171 231 291 351 and 11 21 81 141 201 261 321
rfi.item: Exact restart times for 2-pump vs 6-pump restarts
rfi.reason: Restart timing defines how long system sits unpowered (low-pressure duration) before repressurization
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Apply written rule (D12-D13: 10-sec generator + 30-sec ramp + 30-sec lag) for both Phase 1 and buildout — REASON: written rule is unambiguous; figure treated as illustrative only.

rfi.issue: Surge-protection recommendation clause(s) withheld on p.1, p.2, p.3 (and p.6); type/volume/air-ratio not in available pages, though p.10/p.13 show mitigated Phase 1 max = normal
rfi.item: Surge vessel type, volume and air ratio - Phase 1 and buildout, Turlock and Ceres
rfi.reason: Question explicitly asks for type/size; cannot quote withheld clauses
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Pending full TM, presume bladder-type hydropneumatic surge vessels at/near pump station sized to keep >=10 psi everywhere during 10-sec outage + restart; final volumes/ratios to be pulled from withheld pages or recomputed in later steps — REASON: avoids inventing data silently per rules.

rfi.issue: Pipe design pressure rating / sustained operating pressures not quoted; only 150% surge allowance noted (p.3)
rfi.reason: Needed to judge whether rejoinder surge violates pipe rating
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Judge high-pressure compliance as max transient <= ~normal operating HGL/pressure (per p.10/p.13 notes) — REASON: document states low-pressure mitigation will bring highs close to normal; no rating quoted.

issues.issue: Unit error: document is US units but vessel sizes reported in SI without conversion
issues.item: All alternatives list volumes as m3 total, 50% air (40 m3 air/40 m3 water) from simulator area_m2 x height_m
issues.evidence: Document units: LF-inch (D01-D02 p.1), feet (D04-D06 p.2), gpm-feet (D08-D11 p.2), fps (D15 p.3), mgd/psi (D21-D22/D26 p.3). Rules require use document units. No gallons/ft3 conversion given; final vessel count/conversion deferred to DB team.

issues.issue: Controlling low-pressure result driven by assumed high-point chainage, not surveyed profile
issues.item: 3-segment screening profile; Ceres 141 ft high point assumed 4000 ft from FWPS, Turlock mid-pipe; HIGH-node failures (e.g. SUR-CER-P1-AC80 HIGH 7.5 psi, SUR-CER-BO-AC150 HIGH 2.2 psi)
issues.evidence: Available pages give only elevation 141 ft p.6 and low-res images p.10/p.13; full survey profile withheld. Study notes chainage ASSUMPTION therefore conservative at assumed high point. Cannot confirm vapour location/duration before 10-sec generator p.2.

issues.issue: High-pressure compliance judged without pipe design pressure
issues.item: Claim max stays <= steady / close to normal, steel 150% allowance not binding
issues.evidence: No design pressure rating quoted; only 150% surge allowance noted p.3 and p.10/p.13 max=normal notes. Screening max=steady (e.g. AC80 max=steady) not checked against rating.

issues.issue: Velocity reporting inconsistency; steady vs nominal
issues.item: Capacity table cites nominal velocities 1.608/1.576/4.824/4.728 fps (velocity tool) while SS reruns give 1.63/1.58/4.89/4.73 fps
issues.evidence: velocity tool re-ran 10 mgd/42-in=1.608, 5 mgd/30-in=1.576, 30 mgd/42-in=4.824, 15 mgd/30-in=4.728 confirms nominal; SS flows 7050.9/3473.7/21104.8/10418.3 gpm differ from exact mgd (6944/3472/20833/10416 gpm). Explainable but unnoted.

issues.issue: Unsupported dismissal of open-tank alternative and unsupported cost classes
issues.item: SUR-TUR-BO-ST200 passes 30-56 psi but rejected for ~90 ft height, water-age/contamination, footprint; $100k-$1M / $1M-$10M costs
issues.evidence: No TM costs; costs labelled ASSUMPTION budget analogy. No citation for water-age/contamination criterion beyond general pathogen concern p.2. Height estimate from El 107 ft p.2 vs HGL 198/190 ft p.3 correct arithmetically but footprint/seismic not in record.

findings.evidence: SUR-TUR-P1-NONE-FIX: DIS min 3.04 psi (steady 42.74 psi), SURG 3.03 psi, HIGH -12.48 psi, MID -4.13 psi, max 75.02 psi at DIS; SUR-CER-P1-NONE-FIX: DIS min 3.04 psi (steady 39.21 psi), HIGH -12.01 psi, MID -3.76 psi, max 68.29 psi; SUR-TUR-BO-NONE-FIX: SURG 2.74 psi, HIGH -19.0 psi vapour true, MID -17.09 psi vapour true; SUR-CER-BO-NONE-FIX: SURG 2.58 psi, HIGH -14.49 psi vapour true, MID -13.49 psi. Wave travel exceeds 10-sec generator start (p.2).
findings.limiting_value: 10 psi minimum regulatory margin (p.3); column separation / pathogen intrusion concern (p.2)
findings.modification: Provide surge protection at/near FWPS discharge on each main; generator restart alone (p.2-p.3, Fig.2 p.7) occurs after separation
findings.unit: Turlock 42-in ~41000 ft (p.1) Phase1 10 mgd (p.3) and buildout 30 mgd (p.3); Ceres 30-in ~29000 ft (p.1) Phase1 5 mgd (p.3) and buildout 15 mgd (p.3)

findings.evidence: SS-TUR-P1-FIX: 7051.2 gpm at 91.55 ft TDH vs 7000 gpm at 92 ft (p.2); SS-CER-P1-FIX: 3473.9 gpm at 83.41 ft vs 3500 gpm at 83 ft (p.2); SS-TUR-BO-FIX: 21107 gpm order at 141.51 ft vs 21000 gpm at 142 ft (p.2); SS-CER-BO-FIX: 10419.4 gpm (15.004 mgd) at 132.67 ft vs 10500 gpm at 132 ft (p.2). C=140 (p.3). Nominal velocities (velocity tool): 10 mgd/42-in 1.608 fps; buildout 30 mgd/42-in ~4.8 fps; 5 mgd/30-in ~1.58 fps; 15 mgd/30-in ~4.7 fps. Steady SS velocities 1.63/4.89/1.58/4.73 fps differ only by pumped-flow rounding.
findings.limiting_value: Duty points 3500 gpm at 92/83 ft Phase1 and 142/132 ft buildout (p.2); HGLs 198 ft Turlock / 190 ft Ceres (p.3), clearwell 114 ft (p.2), FWPS El 107 ft (p.2)
findings.modification: Steady-state basis verified; transient screening uses same 3-segment profile

findings.evidence: SUR-TUR-P1-AC30-FIX (30 m3 total, 50% air): SURG min 2.43 psi, HIGH -2.86 psi - fails. SUR-TUR-P1-AC80-FIX (80 m3 total, 50% air): SURG min 13.16 psi (steady 42.73 psi), MID 24.18 psi, HIGH 5.78 psi (steady 26.79 psi), max <=steady at SURG/HIGH/MID. SUR-CER-P1-AC80-FIX: SURG 20.48 psi (steady 39.2 psi), MID 22.36 psi, HIGH 7.51 psi (steady 24.01 psi). SUR-TUR-BO-AC200-FIX (200 m3 total, 50% air): SURG 9.76 psi, MID 23.15 psi, HIGH 3.51 psi. TM notes mitigated max = normal operating pressure (p.10, p.13).
findings.modification: Closed bladder air chambers at FWPS discharge, ~50% air - ASSUMPTION (reason: type/volume/air-ratio withheld; 50% balances feed vs pressure maintenance). Phase1 order ~80 m3 (~2825 ft3 / ~21100 gal total, ~1413 ft3 / ~10570 gal air) per main; buildout phased expansion to ~150-200+ m3 (~5300-7060 ft3 / ~39600-52800 gal total). Final gallons, vessel count and air ratio by DB InfoSurge (p.1) using final survey profile (p.10,p.13 images only in available pages)

findings.evidence: Screening HIGH mins (5.78 psi Turlock P1 AC80, 7.51 psi Ceres P1 AC80, 3.51 psi Turlock BO AC200) driven by ASSUMPTION chainage of 141 ft summit (p.6) (Turlock mid-pipe ~15000 ft, Ceres ~4000 ft from FWPS) - reason: full survey profile withheld except low-res p.10/p.13; elevation 141 ft (p.6) only. TM final-profile mitigated design holds max=normal (p.10,p.13).
findings.limiting_value: 141 ft high point (p.6) vs HGLs 198/190 ft (p.3)
findings.modification: DB team to confirm final profile, lower/shave summit if possible, add combination air/vacuum valves at final summits per AWWA M-11 practice (C=140 per M-11 p.3), add pump inertia/flywheel, expedite restart, re-run InfoSurge before vessel purchase

responses.explanation: Re-ran all underpinning transients with new retrievable labels: SUR-TUR-P1-NONE-FIX, SUR-CER-P1-NONE-FIX, SUR-TUR-BO-NONE-FIX, SUR-CER-BO-NONE-FIX, SUR-TUR-P1-AC30-FIX, SUR-TUR-P1-AC80-FIX, SUR-CER-P1-AC80-FIX, SUR-TUR-BO-AC200-FIX. Old SUR-*-NONE/AC30/AC60/AC80/AC100/AC200/ST200/AC40/AC150 precise mins are withdrawn and replaced by FIX outputs quoted in findings/alternatives. Un-rerun screening sizes (AC60/AC100/AC150/ST200) withdrawn.
responses.issue: All transient surge runs underpinning conclusions are not retrievable; alternatives not actually verified

responses.explanation: Vessel type/volume/air-ratio now explicitly labelled ASSUMPTION with reason (withheld clauses) in findings/alternatives, not cited to pages. Only cited TM facts are max=normal with mitigation (p.10,p.13), 10 psi margin (p.3), and input data.
responses.issue: Recommended surge vessel type/size/volume/air-ratio has no document citation; withheld clauses filled by assumption yet presented as finding

responses.explanation: Volumes now reported in document units: ft3 and gallons (US). SI simulator inputs converted: 30 m3=1060 ft3=7925 gal; 80 m3=2825 ft3=21134 gal (40 m3 air=1413 ft3=10567 gal); 200 m3=7063 ft3=52834 gal. Simulator area_m2 x height_m retained only as run parameter.
responses.issue: Unit error: document is US units but vessel sizes reported in SI without conversion

responses.explanation: Confirmed: screening uses 3-segment profile ASSUMPTION (clearwell 114 ft p.2, El 107 ft p.2, HGLs 198/190 ft p.3, 141 ft summit p.6, lengths ~41000/~29000 ft p.1, C=140 p.3). Chainage assumed. HIGH-node results flagged conservative; final vapour location/duration requires DB full-profile InfoSurge (p.1) and survey (p.10,p.13). Protection conclusion (need vessels) does not depend on chainage - unprotected header also fails.
responses.issue: Controlling low-pressure result driven by assumed high-point chainage, not surveyed profile

responses.explanation: No pipe design pressure in available pages; high-pressure finding limited to screening max<=steady with vessels and TM max=normal notes (p.10,p.13) plus steel context. DB to verify highs <= design rating / surge allowance during final InfoSurge.
responses.issue: High-pressure compliance judged without pipe design pressure

responses.explanation: Nominal velocities (velocity tool: 10 mgd/42-in 1.608 fps etc.) are exact-mgd values; SS velocities (1.63/1.58/4.89/4.73 fps) reflect simulated pumped flows (7051/3474/21107/10419 gpm vs exact 6944/3472/20833/10417 gpm). Difference is rounding/duty-point residual, now noted.
responses.issue: Velocity reporting inconsistency; steady vs nominal

responses.explanation: Open-tank alternative withdrawn (no retrievable ST run). Costs set to n/a - no costs in available pages. Height arithmetic (HGL 198/190 ft p.3 vs El 107 ft p.2) retained only as context; water-age/footprint/seismic not claimed as TM criteria beyond general pathogen/pressurized-flow concern (p.2).
